title: Collections Standard for Independent Living Residency Agreement Accounts — Late Fees and Goodwill Waivers
content:
Monthly fees under the Independent Living Residency Agreement fall due on the fee due day and may be paid without penalty during the grace period.

## Clauses in force

**L1 — Grace period.** A late fee may be assessed only after the grace period of the apartment type has passed since the monthly fee charge for that billing period was posted. The grace period ends at the end of the day equal to the posting date of the monthly fee charge plus the grace days in calendar days, and a late fee may be assessed only on a later date.

**L2 — Minimum.** No late fee is assessed when the past-due amount of the billing period is below the minimum past-due amount of the apartment type.

**L3 — One per period.** At most one late fee is assessed per residency per billing period.

**L4 — Status.** A late fee may be assessed only while the residency is in active or notice given status.

**L5 — Goodwill waiver.** On the resident's request a late fee may be waived as goodwill with a late fee waiver credit of the full late fee amount referencing that late fee entry, provided the past-due fees of that billing period have since been paid in full.

**L6 — Waiver availability.** A goodwill waiver is available only while the number of late fee waiver credits posted on the residency within the rolling 365 calendar days ending on the handling date is below the goodwill waiver allowance of the apartment type, and the number of returned payments posted on the residency within the same rolling 365 days is zero.

**L7 — Excluded charges.** Late fees are never charged on unpaid late fees, community fees or one-time service fees.

## Retired clauses

- The clause under which the past-due amount was the period past-due measure for that billing period is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for reckoning the past-due amount.
- The clause under which the late fee was otherwise the greater of the flat late fee and the late fee percentage of the past-due amount, rounded to the cent half up, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the late fee amount.

## The grace clock at its boundary (hypothetical; 10 grace days)

| Monthly fee charge posted | Grace period ends | Earliest day a late fee may be assessed |
|---|---|---|
| The 1st of the month | End of the 11th | The 12th |
| The 3rd of the month | End of the 13th | The 14th |

A late fee assessed on the 11th, for a charge posted on the 1st, falls inside the grace period and is not permitted.

## Goodwill waiver — truth table

| Past-due fees of that period since paid in full | Waiver credits in the rolling 365 days below the allowance | Returned payments in the rolling 365 days | Waiver available on request |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Zero | Yes |
| Yes | No | Any | No |
| Yes | Yes | One or more | No |
| No | Any | Any | No |

A waiver, when given, is a credit of the full late fee amount, never a part of it, and references the late fee entry it waives.

superseded_clauses: The past-due amount is independent_msr_period_past_due for that billing period
Otherwise the late fee is the greater of late_fee_flat and late_fee_pct percent of the past-due amount rounded to the cent half up.
